results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 69 aligned units' outline summaries match the controlling idea of their spec paragraph in spec order (p01-p69, with the verticals section p51-p52 after Six Axes as the spec orders it, and p46 before p45 in the register section as the spec orders it). The five opening callouts are not spec paragraphs and are matched to null; they summarise the thesis and supporting claims and add no off-spec idea.

The only unit the outliner marked two_ideas is the scope paragraph (horizontal vs vertical + margins). The margin figures are the evidence the spec assigns to this paragraph (p21 evidence: 'Scope and seller mix change margins') and the controlling idea itself says 'their economics differ sharply'; the second 'idea' is the support for the first, not a separate claim. All other units were marked single-idea.

Every unit ties to a supporting claim: scene and register (T1, T5), Four Models and Six Axes (T2, T1), Vertical Differences and What Each Model Asks (T3), In Practice patterns 1-4 (T4), Trade-offs, Failure Modes, Chief Architect's View and Questions (T5, T3), conclusion (synthesis of T1-T5). The software-for-professionals paragraph supports T2 by bounding the ladder. No orphan paragraph found.

Every quotation, statistic, table and figure is followed or framed by a sentence saying what it shows: e.g. Adevinta revenue mix ('years into a declared transactional push'), Facebook 2016 quote ('states the model in a single sentence'), OLX LTR labels, Zillow variable consideration ('cannot price on sales without building an attribution pipeline first'), the register table ('Read across the rows and Noor's proposal shrinks'), the trade-off table ('Two judgements follow'), Figures 1-4 by captions stating the point, the three managed retreats by 'The common thread is...'. The lead-generation pricing list is framed by its lead sentence and labelled bullets; acceptable.

results.quote: What to watch at group level: the share of contacts, leads and orders per profile
results.finding: Declared conclusion_summary carrying 'the four decisions' and introducing 'the signals that show whether they hold'. The paragraph opens on a new list with no reference to the four decisions, and its close ties the signals to endpoint changes, not to whether the decisions hold. The section opener ('Four matter most.') also does not announce the things to watch that the section's controlling idea includes, so the paragraph arrives unannounced. Rewrite the boundary sentence to say these are the signals that show the four decisions are holding.

All other declared transitions are expressed at their boundaries: e.g. p02 'therefore' (cause_effect), p05 'Ingrid did not argue with the slide' (contrast), p06 'By the end of the afternoon' (time), p11 'Because the platform never sees the money' (cause_effect), p19 'not on the ladder' (contrast), p21 'The second axis in the table' (sequence), verticals 'The six axes also explain' (elaboration), asks 'the endpoint reaches furthest' (emphasis), in-practice 'What each rung adds is what a marketplace takes on, or gives up' (elaboration), register 'Veldmark applied the lesson of category gating' (cause_effect), p37 'None of these brands' (contrast), p41 'The common thread' (summary), trade-offs 'bring every marketplace leadership team back to one question' (cause_effect), Chief Architect 'The seven failures share a remedy' (problem_solution), conclusion callback, p69 contrast 'It does not tell it whether'. Failure Modes ('The taxonomy fails in practice') carries the contrast implicitly through 'in practice' after the prescriptions; acceptable.

results.quote: First the vocabulary: after the grid that split Veldmark's four brands into twenty country-and-category rows, it defines four models
results.finding: Both readers describe the declared organising principle (vocabulary, consequences, judgement; prerequisite order) and place every section clearly. But both lost the thread at the roadmap: 'the grid' and Veldmark are referred to as known before the scene introduces them, and the clause in front of the three-part list forced a re-read (A item 1: 'assume the reader already knows the grid and Veldmark... I re-read it'). The order is fine; the prose presumes the scene. Reword the roadmap to promise the grid ('starting from a grid that splits...') rather than refer back to it.
results.corroborated_by: flow-reader-B, section 3 item 1 ('refers to "the grid" as if I already knew it... I had to read it twice')

results.quote: Two documented products show single cells of this table turned into product rules
results.finding: Both readers had to re-read this opening sentence; 'single cells ... turned into product rules' is abstract and only becomes clear from the examples (A item 3). The position is fine; the opening sentence should say plainly what the two products show (e.g. that a vertical's billing unit and its seller split became product boundaries).
results.corroborated_by: flow-reader-B, section 3 item 5 ('I had to re-read this to see what "single cells ... turned into product rules" meant')

results.draft_locus: What Each Model Asks of the Architecture ¶1
results.quote: Of the axes in the vertical table, the endpoint reaches furthest into the systems
results.finding: Both readers paused at this seam: coming from the vertical detour, 'the axes in the vertical table' points at the wrong table (the axes were defined in the six-axes table) and does not say the chapter is returning to the endpoint ladder (A item 4: 'it points at the wrong table'). Both readers judge the section order sound (it matches the roadmap and the spec's prerequisite rationale), so the fault is the bridge sentence, not the order.
results.corroborated_by: flow-reader-B, section 3 item 6 ('This is the weakest seam... I paused to place where I was')

results.draft_locus: Setting the Scene at Veldmark: One Group, Four Models ¶5
results.quote: and the group ran at least four
results.finding: Reader A tried to match Veldmark's 'four models' to the ladder's four (classifieds, lead generation, transactional, managed) and could not: Veldmark has no managed profile and Keybridge is 'not a marketplace at all'. The chapter never says which four Veldmark runs, so the same number names two different sets. The heading is fixed by the spec, but the prose can name the four (e.g. classifieds, transactional goods, dealer leads, agency leads, plus SaaS).

results.draft_locus: Trade-offs: Where Should the Marketplace End? ¶2
results.quote: they are the author's, as a Chief Architect
results.finding: Reader B stopped to check whether 'I' was Ingrid (the Group Chief Architect throughout) or the author; the same at 'A rule I use' in the Chief Architect's View. The first-person voice is in the spec; the collision comes from 'as a Chief Architect', which the prose can disambiguate.

results.quote: trust and safety and a product catalog with entitlements
results.finding: Reader B briefly read 'product catalog' as the catalog of items (the item-identity axis's 'catalog products') rather than the catalog of paid products, and met the same ambiguity again in the Chief Architect's View ('the product catalog and entitlements'). A qualifier (paid-product catalog) removes it.

results.draft_locus: What Each Model Asks of the Architecture ¶1 (table, Trust focus row)
results.quote: Valuation error, adverse selection, condition fraud
results.finding: 'Adverse selection' is a marketplace-economics term (the audience's does_not_know includes marketplace economics) used undefined in the consequences table and explained only later in Pattern 3 ('sellers whose homes are overvalued accept while the rest walk away (adverse selection)'). Define it at first use or drop it from the table cell.
results.corroborated_by: flow-reader-B, section 3 item 4 ('the chapter defines it after it has used it')

results.finding: Other terms are defined at first use: liquidity (callout), listing marketplace, endpoint, VAS, ARPA/ARPR, GMV, take rate, trader, VIN, provisions, KYB/KYC, true-ups, entitlements, learning to rank, DSA and DAC7 (named before the table, explained after), PSP, EMI, principal revenue. Reader B's other items do not fail: 'Re-Commerce' is a segment name the stated audience (leaders of recommerce marketplaces) knows; 'read path' is architecture vocabulary the audience has; 'estimation risk on success fees' follows from the pay-at-close paragraph just before the ladder table. No does_not_know item (network effects, multi-homing, percolation, hybrid retrieval, P2B, statements of reasons) is used without being given.

Opens on the declared puzzling scenario (five people, five partly right answers), not a placeholder, restated question, dictionary definition, 'dawn of man' or book report; p02 states a disputable thesis and p03 a roadmap.

Does not open with 'in conclusion', is not a bare restatement or grab bag, and adds no body evidence; the liquidity paragraph is the declared hand-off (contrast: where the job ends vs whether it is done well), not a new subtopic developed in the conclusion.

Synthesis no single section states: the five opening answers each map to particular register rows, so the disagreement becomes configuration. So-what given: 'Shared platforms are sized by the profiles that need them, and each move along the ladder is a category-gated bet with an exit plan, reversed by changing a row rather than by a migration program.'

Returns to the five people's five answers and assigns each to rows: 'classifieds' to Tradeyard Portugal, 'becoming transactional' to three Safe Deal profiles, 'dealer subscriptions' to Motorvane, 'advertising and visibility' to paid products, the messaging platform to every contact-ending profile.

The cold reader predicted all ten expected sections in order (grid; endpoint ladder; five axes and profile; profiles by vertical; what each model asks of the systems; documented moves both ways; Veldmark's register; where to end; failure modes; Chief Architect's standing decisions and questions), the evidence (dated documented industry cases and the fictional Veldmark) and the tone. Its hesitation about whether the grid is presented here is covered by the flow_is_followable failure on the same roadmap sentence.

The reader named the added order, payment, payout, shipping, dispute and ledger contexts through a licensed PSP, KYC and trader traceability, DAC7 reporting, buyer protection as a provisioned liability, and the change in ranking signal to purchase; and scoped the move per category and country (goods, not cars or homes, as leboncoin, Kleinanzeigen and Marktplaats did), as configuration in a versioned profile register, as a bet with an exit plan and a cheap retreat. Everything in the expected answer is present; OLX's pull-back is implied by the exit plan rather than named, which does not change the outcome.
